issue.title: Pinhole 2D view has focal issue when projecting 3d with undistorted images, but world works

repository.name: rerun
repository.description: Visualize, query, and stream to train on multimodal robotics data.

issue.body:
<!--
First look if there is already a similar bug report. If there is, upvote the issue with 👍
-->

**Describe the bug**
With some pinhole model, 3d projection on image plane is buggy. At first I thought it was a problem of my matrices, but no this is really a bug in the viewer. The "world view" gives correct results.

**To Reproduce**
Here are my 2 rrd files:
- The buggy one: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HF04o7kvnwB60SkwMPAinXIB5NULduYF/view?usp=sharing,
- The one working: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1N3Esx-GE9TE9scu5p-PR287N9hwQgsd8/view?usp=sharing

The data has been produced from public panoptic dataset. The first file uses an undistort alpha of 0.0 and produce buggy visualization. The second file uses an undistort alpha of 1.0 and produce good result.

I have no idea what is causing that, as I can only see this problem in rerun viewer.

**Expected behavior**
The focal to be correct

**Screenshots**
Undistort 0, as you can see all 3d keypoints and bboxes are "off":
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1d2f7d7-100d-43cd-afd9-d8d435dad78c)

Undistort 1:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd37232a-1004-4266-bd3a-98bef64c0a5c)

As a proof this is a problem in the 2d view, when tracing a ray it's correctly going on the 3d model:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ff64337-b1b4-43bb-aabb-d2ff4cf13c31)

**Rerun version**
0.23

data.body:
```
rr.log(
    cam_entity,
    rr.Pinhole(image_from_camera=K, width=image_np.shape[1], height=image_np.shape[0]),
)
```

Where K is the standard 
```
| fx 0 cx|
| 0 fy c |
| 0 0  1 |
```

Still hitting this issue in `0.33.0`. Would love to see a fix soon! See below for vibecoded minimal reproduction of the issue. It logs: * a `Pinhole` * green explicit `Points2D` computed from the same K matrix * red camera-frame `Points3D` that should be natively projected into the `Spatial2DView` The script generates three cases: 1. `square`: `fx=fy=360` — native-projected red `Points3D` are visible and align with green `Points2D` 2. `nonsquare`: `fx=300`, `fy=420` — green `Points2D` are visible, but native-projected red `Points3D` are missing/invisible 3. `equalized`: `fx=fy=sqrt(300*420)` — native-projected red `Points3D` become visible again and align with green `Points2D` This seems to reproduce the `fx != fy` failure in a minimal abstract camera setup. I can't attach the `.rrd` files but here are the screenshots: **equalized** **nonsquare** **square** Script: ``` # repro_rerun_fx_fy_projection_bug.py # # Minimal no-image repro for native 3D->2D pinhole projection with fx != fy. # # Setup: # uv init # uv add rerun-sdk==0.33.0 numpy # # Generate RRDs: # uv run python repro_rerun_fx_fy_projection_bug.py # # Generate RRDs + screenshots: # uv run python repro_rerun_fx_fy_projection_bug.py --screenshots # # Open manually: # uv run rerun rerun_fx_fy_repro_outputs/repro_rerun_fx_fy_square.rrd # uv run rerun rerun_fx_fy_repro_outputs/repro_rerun_fx_fy_nonsquare.rrd # uv run rerun rerun_fx_fy_repro_outputs/repro_rerun_fx_fy_equalized.rrd import argparse import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import rerun as rr import rerun.blueprint as rrb WIDTH = 512 HEIGHT = 384 CAMERA_FRAME = "camera" IMAGE_FRAME = "image_pixels" ROOT = "/repro" PINHOLE = f"{ROOT}/pinhole" EXPECTED_UV = f"{PINHOLE}/expected_uv" POINTS_3D = f"{ROOT}/points3d_camera_frame" CASES = ("square", "nonsquare", "equalized") def intrinsics(case: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]: """Return abstract calibrated pinhole intrinsics for a 512x384 image plane.""" cx = WIDTH / 2.0 cy = HEIGHT / 2.0 if case == "square": return 360.0, 360.0, cx, cy if case == "nonsquare": return 300.0, 420.0, cx, cy if case == "equalized": # Same rough focal scale as the nonsquare case, but with fx == fy. f = float(np.sqrt(300.0 * 420.0)) return f, f, cx, cy raise ValueError(case) def camera_points() -> np.ndarray: """Asymmetric camera-frame points in front of the camera.""" return np.array( [ [0.00, 0.00, 1.0], [0.15, 0.00, 1.0], [0.00, 0.08, 1.0], [0.15, 0.08, 1.0], ], dtype=np.float32, ) def project(points_xyz: np.ndarray, fx: float, fy: float, cx: float, cy: float) -> np.ndarray: """Manual pinhole projection used for the explicit green Points2D reference.""" x = points_xyz[:, 0] y = points_xyz[:, 1] z = points_xyz[:, 2] return np.stack([fx * x / z + cx, fy * y / z + cy], axis=-1) def make_blueprint(case: str) -> rrb.Blueprint: return rrb.Blueprint( rrb.Spatial2DView( name=f"2D pinhole projection: {case}", origin=PINHOLE, contents=[ EXPECTED_UV, POINTS_3D, ], ), rrb.Spatial3DView( name="3D scene", origin=ROOT, contents=[f"{ROOT}/**"], ), collapse_panels=True, ) def log_scene(rec: rr.RecordingStream, case: str) -> None: fx, fy, cx, cy = intrinsics(case) points = camera_points() uv = project(points, fx, fy, cx, cy).astype(np.float32) k = np.array( [ [fx, 0.0, cx], [0.0, fy, cy], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], ], dtype=np.float64, ) rec.log( PINHOLE, rr.Pinhole( image_from_camera=k, resolution=[WIDTH, HEIGHT], camera_xyz=rr.ViewCoordinates.RDF, parent_frame=CAMERA_FRAME, child_frame=IMAGE_FRAME, ), static=True, ) rec.log(PINHOLE, rr.CoordinateFrame(IMAGE_FRAME), static=True) # Large green explicit 2D reference projection, computed directly from K. # This acts as the visible underlay/target. rec.log( EXPECTED_UV, rr.Points2D( uv, colors=np.tile(np.array([[0, 255, 0]], dtype=np.uint8), (len(uv), 1)), radii=rr.Radius.ui_points(12.0), ), static=True, ) rec.log(EXPECTED_UV, rr.CoordinateFrame(IMAGE_FRAME), static=True) # Smaller red 3D camera-frame points, outside the pinhole subtree. # When native projection works, these should appear centered inside # the larger green expected-UV reference dots. rec.log( POINTS_3D, rr.Points3D( points, colors=np.tile(np.array([[255, 0, 0]], dtype=np.uint8), (len(points), 1)), radii=rr.Radius.ui_points(5.0), ), static=True, ) rec.log(POINTS_3D, rr.CoordinateFrame(CAMERA_FRAME), static=True) rec.send_blueprint(make_blueprint(case)) print(f"{case}: fx={fx:.3f}, fy={fy:.3f}, cx={cx:.3f}, cy={cy:.3f}, fx/fy={fx / fy:.3f}") print(f"{case}: expected_uv =") print(uv) def write_rrd(case: str, out_dir: Path) -> Path: out_path = out_dir / f"repro_rerun_fx_fy_{case}.rrd" rec = rr.RecordingStream(f"rerun_pinhole_fx_fy_repro_{case}") rec.save(str(out_path)) log_scene(rec, case) rec.disconnect() return out_path def write_headless_screenshot(rrd_path: Path, out_png: Path, rerun_bin: str | None = None) -> Path: rerun_exe = rerun_bin or shutil.which("rerun") if rerun_exe is None: raise RuntimeError( "Could not find `rerun` executable on PATH. " "Try running with `uv run`, or pass --rerun-bin /path/to/rerun." ) cmd = [ rerun_exe, "--headless", "--window-size", "1200x800", "--screenshot-to", str(out_png), str(rrd_path), ] print("Running:", " ".join(cmd)) subprocess.run(cmd, check=True) return out_png def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument( "--case", choices=[*CASES, "all"], default="all", help="Which case to generate. Default: all.", ) parser.add_argument( "--out-dir", type=Path, default=Path("rerun_fx_fy_repro_outputs"), help="Output directory for RRDs and PNGs.", ) parser.add_argument( "--screenshots", action="store_true", help="Also save screenshots using `rerun --headless --screenshot-to`.", ) parser.add_argument( "--rerun-bin", type=str, default=None, help="Optional path to the Rerun viewer binary. Defaults to `rerun` on PATH.", ) args = parser.parse_args() args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) cases = CASES if args.case == "all" else (args.case,) print(f"Writing outputs to: {args.out_dir.resolve()}") print() for case in cases: rrd_path = write_rrd(case, args.out_dir) print(f"Wrote RRD: {rrd_path}") if args.screenshots: png_path = write_headless_screenshot( rrd_path=rrd_path, out_png=args.out_dir / f"repro_rerun_fx_fy_{case}.png", rerun_bin=args.rerun_bin, ) print(f"Wrote PNG: {png_path}") print() print("Expected visual result:") print(" square: large green Points2D visible; small red native-projected Points3D visible inside them") print(" nonsquare: large green Points2D visible; small red native-projected Points3D missing/invisible") print(" equalized: large green Points2D visible; small red native-projected Points3D visible inside them") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` The key observation is that the `nonsquare` case differs only in `fx/fy`; the points, coordinate frames, blueprint, and explicit 2D reference projection are otherwise identical.
+1 this issue is an important bug

I just ran into the same issue today in Rerun 0.36.0 . Looking at https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/11076, it seems like this is a known issue. 😢

Right now my temporary workaround is to warp my camera images so that the effective `fx ~= fy`, similar to what OP suggested. The positions of 2D entities will need to be shifted correspondingly (e.g. `Points2D`), but at least the projection is working again in the viewer. Still, it'd be great if we can get a warning when it can't project the 3D entities, and it'd be even better if Rerun can fully support anamorphic pinhole cameras in the future :)
